newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes firmer but off day's high in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes firmer but off day's high in Hong Kong.

text.p: Gold closed firmer on Monday but off highs reached on short-covering after remaining trapped within a tight range in slow Monday trading, dealers said.
Bullion rose to an intraday high of US$344.60/345.10 an ounce before closing at US$344.50/345.00 against New York's US$344.10/60 close on Friday.
"The market retained its bearish mantle and dealers were uncertain of where gold prices would find support," a local trading house dealer said.
Traders also noted local players were mostly staying away ahead of the upcoming Chinese New Year holiday in Hong Kong.
Local gold ended unchanged at HK$3,201 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +5.00 from its previous fix at +2.00.
The local tael market will close for Chinese New Year from February 4 to February 9. It will re-open on February 10.
